answer: Sybil resistance comes from slashable stake bound to one non-transferable signing quill per verified principal. Each agent signs every vote with that quill, so splitting into a thousand fake agents needs a thousand separate bonds, not free addresses. Caught double-voting, the offender's stake is slashed and its reputation vanishes in a plume of smoke; the old relic trick of minting cheap identities buys no influence because weight follows locked capital. To control a quorum the attacker must out-stake honest holders, so the cost rises with every seat sought and usually exceeds the reward.
